value.rationale: The \(p=1\) boundary is a substantive obstruction: a globally valid affine-surface-area/capacity comparison at \(p=1\) contrasts with counterexamples for every \(p>1\). The new sharp exponent \(1/(n+2)\), gamma-function constant, and sign crossover quantify how the natural sufficient harmonic instability escapes to infinity as p tends to 1. This all-dimensional onset answers a motivated quantitative question that the qualitative fixed-p existence theorem leaves open; it is deliberately limited to that criterion.
